title: Employee Headcount by Salary Band
description:
Count the number of employees in each salary band: `'Under 50K'` (< 50,000), `'50K-75K'` (50,000–74,999), `'75K-100K'` (75,000–99,999), and `'Over 100K'` (≥ 100,000).

**Table: employees** — `employee_id`, `name`, `salary`

Output columns: `salary_band`, `headcount`. Order by minimum salary in each band (ascending).
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (employee_id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, salary DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice',45000),(2,'Bob',62000),(3,'Charlie',78000),(4,'Diana',95000),(5,'Eve',110000),(6,'Frank',48000),(7,'Grace',55000),(8,'Henry',85000),(9,'Iris',125000),(10,'Jack',72000),(11,'Karen',68000),(12,'Liam',92000);
solution_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN salary < 50000 THEN 'Under 50K' WHEN salary < 75000 THEN '50K-75K' WHEN salary < 100000 THEN '75K-100K' ELSE 'Over 100K' END AS salary_band, COUNT(*) AS headcount FROM employees GROUP BY CASE WHEN salary < 50000 THEN 'Under 50K' WHEN salary < 75000 THEN '50K-75K' WHEN salary < 100000 THEN '75K-100K' ELSE 'Over 100K' END ORDER BY MIN(salary);

test_cases.description: Under 50K: 2 (Alice, Frank); 50K-75K: 4 (Bob, Grace, Jack, Karen); 75K-100K: 4 (Charlie, Diana, Henry, Liam); Over 100K: 2 (Eve, Iris)

hints: Use a CASE WHEN expression that checks thresholds from lowest to highest in the SELECT and GROUP BY.
ORDER BY MIN(salary) within each group produces the natural low-to-high ordering of bands.
The same CASE WHEN expression must appear verbatim in both SELECT and GROUP BY.
explanation: 'Under 50K': Alice (45K), Frank (48K) = 2. '50K-75K': Bob (62K), Grace (55K), Jack (72K), Karen (68K) = 4. '75K-100K': Charlie (78K), Diana (95K), Henry (85K), Liam (92K) = 4. 'Over 100K': Eve (110K), Iris (125K) = 2. Four distinct salary bands.
